summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and a history of mitral valve replacement was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure with severe bilateral leg edema and shortness of breath. She had been nonadherent with her torsemide, leading to fluid overload. She was treated with aggressive IV diuresis, transitioned to high-dose oral torsemide and metolazone, and managed for hyperkalemia and uncontrolled diabetes. A right heart catheterization confirmed elevated biventricular filling pressures. She received a course of antibiotics for suspected HCAP, which resolved. Her left heel ulcer was stable, and no active infection was found. Despite improvement, she chose to leave against medical advice due to a recent hypoglycemic episode, after demonstrating understanding of the risks. She was discharged home with services on increased diuretics, warfarin, insulin, and multiple comorbid medications, with close follow-up arranged.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
